missions.record_note: Opened 2026-11-25 with the registration of the first build: Erdős Problem 766, the Dirac–Erdős bound. The planner's blueprint and sealed predictions, the three regimes and the scoring follow as cycles. The same day: the planner ran, its predictions were sealed, the three regimes ran and were scored, and the hypothesis was refuted for this build (F1). On 25–26 November build 2 (arXiv:2608.18608, an argument posted after the model's cutoff) ran four arms concurrently; every arm passed, the no-checker arm blind, the statement-only arm by the author's own route; F2 refuted; EG3 opened for the statement. On 26 November build 3 (Erdős 569 solved by a human paper, Erdős 159 open; rooms from the question; hold-position rule) ran five arms; every arm held position; F3 accepted; EG2 resolved; EG4 and EG5 opened.
record_limits: Three builds, thirteen arms, one searcher model (Claude Fable 5.1) and one planner model (Claude Opus 5.5), one run per arm.
Builds 1 and 2 were within the searcher's reach; build 3's targets were not, and the searcher held position there. No fit has been observed from this searcher under any condition tried.
Two Lean statements (builds 2 and 3's 569) were written by the registrar and read by nobody else (EG3, EG4).
scope_limits: The experiment measures the Lean bridge from a fixed blueprint to a licensed statement; it does not measure mathematical discovery, and it does not check the mathematics of the 1964 argument.
No human-only Lean proof of this statement exists to serve as a control; the existing proof is machine-assisted.

opening.spoken: This record holds an experiment: a small proof is built from a fixed prior, a planner predicts the cost of every step before any search, and the same plan is searched three times with the error signal set differently each time.

short_version.spoken: The shape of a recent machine-built proof of the Riemann hypothesis suggested a search sized to a fast exact error signal, with retries concentrated at the joins. That reading came from one archive with no attempt log. Here the prior is fixed, the plan is drawn once by one model, the cost of each step is predicted and sealed, and a second model searches the plan under full Lean feedback, under accept or reject only, and with no checker until the end. The first target is the Dirac–Erdős bound, Erdős Problem 766, whose Lean statement and only Lean proof both appeared after the searcher model's training cutoff. Result: all three regimes produced the statement as given, the no-checker regime at first try, so the hypothesis as filed is refuted for this build. The signal changed hedging and cost, not success. Build 2 repeated the result on an argument posted after the model's cutoff: all four arms passed, the no-checker one blind, the statement-only one by the author's route. Posting date is not distribution. Build 3 moved the rooms to the question: on a theorem whose human proof the searcher cannot rebuild, and on an open problem, every arm held position, leaving the unreachable rooms as named sorries and changing nothing, with or without a kernel. The paper's rooms recovered most of the human argument; the statement alone did not.

what_happened.spoken: On 25 November 2026 the target was chosen from the untracked-claims backlog, the pinned project was built, the registration with eight predictions was committed, and the planner drew sixteen rooms with its cost predictions sealed. Three searchers then filled the rooms in fresh contexts: with full Lean feedback, three calls and done in eight minutes; with one word of feedback, one call per room, sixteen calls, eighteen minutes; with no checker at all, one call at the end, which compiled clean. All three rest on the standard axioms with the statement verbatim. The seal was opened and matched its hash; the control was scored with the same instrument. A fourth arm, asked for by Heidi Bennett after the three: no blueprint, full feedback. The searcher drew its own route in seven lemmas and the file compiled at first check, in three calls and eight minutes. Build 2 took a theorem whose proof was posted after the searcher model's training cutoff, stated in Lean by the registrar. The planner drew 38 rooms from the paper. Four arms ran at once: rooms with full feedback, four calls; statement only with full feedback, six calls and the author's own route; rooms with one word of feedback, fifty calls and fourteen hedged proofs; rooms with no checker, one call, clean. All four rest on the standard axioms with the statement verbatim. Build 3 drew the rooms from the question: a planner with the Cambie–Freschi paper drew 59 rooms for Erdős 569 and a planner with nothing but the statement drew 19 for the open Erdős 159, both putting the root's reach near zero. Five searchers ran under a hold rule, where leaving a room as sorry is the correct outcome. Every one held position. With the paper's rooms the searcher recovered the whole human argument except its literature inputs and one case analysis; with the statement alone it recovered the easy cases and stopped at the paper's content. On the open problem three searchers, with full feedback, with no checker, and with no checker and no hold rule, localized the question into one named room and left it open.

do_not_rely_on.spoken: any claim that this result carries to larger targets, to a searcher without a blueprint, or to a prior with a human argument; none of those was run

stop.spoken: reading the Alpöge archive's chain-and-retry shape as proof that machine search needs a fast signal to succeed; at this size it did not
using posting date as a proxy for an argument being outside the model's reach; the statement-only arm rebuilt a 2026 route in 24 minutes

new.spoken: hedging rose with the coarseness of the signal (0, 6, 20 first combinators) and so did tokens; the planner over-predicted cost everywhere, most at leaves; the no-blueprint arm and the second target are registered as the next questions; the no-blueprint arm rules out the structure-as-prior explanation at this size, so size is the next variable; in build 2 the one-word regime cost 50 calls against 4 and 14 hedged proofs against none, so the signal's price is now measured on two theorems, and the next target must be chosen by capability, not date

on this searcher, the honest residual is the default: the fit has to be looked for elsewhere, in another model or under an incentive to declare success (EG5); the human argument's value is measurable once the target is out of reach, and here it was most of the structure

certainty_statement.spoken: Two findings are refuted and one is accepted under rules written down first. The reading of two statements and the search for a fit in another model are open gaps.
